Plausible broken app that could pass: none found that this row could miss; row 18 concerns the golden only. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app (like this golden) whose candidate page has no explicit 'close conversation' state could see U's 'Rafael's message shows as not seen' leg depend on how the judge 'moves Tomas off' the conversation (see residual risk 1).

Residual risks (why risk=true, not a defect finding):
1. hro_seen first leg depends on judge navigation: the candidate UI has no close control; openId persists when the 'My applications' nav button is clicked (threads.js:215-219), and catchUp marks read while the pane is active and at bottom (threads.js:157). If the judge 'moves Tomas to his applications list' by clicking that nav button instead of reloading (candidate openId resets to null on load, threads.js:7) or opening his Data Analyst conversation, Rafael's new message becomes Seen immediately and the oracle could lose hro_seen (weight 1.5). Spec-conformant behaviour, feasible path exists.
2. Nav total badge is computed before the async catchUp/markRead (app.js:113-121 vs threads.js:212), so the total can briefly show +1 until the POST /read broadcast refresh; the protocol's 15-second snapshot makes this benign.
3. Not measured: no full configured judge run, no Oracle score, no visual likert measurement; hro_pol_failed_send, the UI path of protocol U's candidate-off-conversation step and many replay-status legs were verified only by source reading or API-level script. 'Plausibly satisfies' is supported; 'the oracle can score high' is not measured.
